questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A) The International Labour Organization's key objective.
B) The basic social protection for the most vulnerable.

explain.定位:
The International Labour Organization says the number of people without jobs is increasing.
In its latest update on global employment trends, the agency says projections of the number of
unemployed people this year range from 210 million to nearly 240 million people.
国际劳工组织表示，失业人数正在增加。在其关于全球就业趋势的最新报告中，该机构称今
年失业人数的预测值在 2.1 亿到将近 2.4 亿人之间。
explain.信号:
新闻首句总述即主题落点。新闻开头第一句 the number of people without jobs is
increasing 就抛出核心事实「失业人数在增加」，紧接着全段都在围绕失业数字与影响展
开。新闻的主题信号通常落在开头总述句，这里正是如此。
explain.替换:
the number of people without jobs is increasing ↔ Rising unemployment worldwide
同义改写：失业人数增加等于失业上升
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
The International Labour Organization's key objective. 借用了录音第二段 Its key
objective is to place at the center of recovery efforts 的原词 key objective，听到这个
词容易心动；但它只是结尾介绍那份就业协议时一笔带过的细节，不是整篇主题，犯了以局
部细节冒充主旨的错。
借用原文：Its key objective is to place at the center of recovery efforts
B) 原词陷阱
The basic social protection for the most vulnerable. 几乎照搬录音第二段 provide
basic social protection for the most vulnerable 的原词，听到极易选；但它讲的是那份
就业协议的具体内容之一，是细节，不是这则新闻整体在讲的「失业上升」。
借用原文：provide basic social protection for the most vulnerable
D) 原词陷阱
Global economic recovery. 借了录音 it takes four to five years after economic
recovery 里的 economic recovery 一词；但原文只是顺带提「经济复苏后还要四五年失业
才回落」，整篇主题是失业问题，不是复苏本身，方向上反而和主旨错位。
借用原文：it takes four to five years after economic recovery

questions.stem: What does Juan Somavia, Director-General of the International Labour Organization say?
options: A) Many countries have not taken measures to create enough jobs.
B) Few countries know how to address the current economic crisis.
C) Few countries have realized the seriousness of the current crisis.
D) Many countries need support to improve their people's livelihood.

explain.定位:
The Director-General of the International Labour Organization Juan Somavia notes that some
countries have taken measures to address the effects of the global crisis. However, he points
out that many countries have not done so.
国际劳工组织总干事胡安·索马维亚指出，一些国家已采取措施应对全球危机的影响。然而，
他强调，许多国家并没有这样做。
explain.信号:
人名出现加转折 However 后才是落点。答案句由两个信号共同锁定：先听到人名 Juan
Somavia，紧跟其观点；再遇转折词 However，转折之后的「许多国家没这么做」才是他
真正要强调的重点。前半「some countries 已采取措施」是铺垫，转折后才是落点。
explain.替换:
many countries have not done so ↔
Many countries have not taken measures to create enough jobs
代词还原：done so 等于 taken measures
some countries have taken measures to address the effects of the global crisis ↔
create enough jobs
上下文补全：所采取的措施即针对就业
explain.排除:
B) 偷换概念
Few countries know how to address the current economic crisis. 借了录音里的
address 与 crisis 等词，听着耳熟；但原文说的是许多国家「没去做（not done so）」，
不是「很少国家不知道怎么做」。它既把 many 偷换成 few，又把「没采取行动」偷换成
「不懂方法」，答非所问。
借用原文：address the effects of the global crisis
C) 未提及
Few countries have realized the seriousness of the current crisis. 蹭了 crisis 一词，可
原文只谈各国「有没有采取措施」，从没说各国「是否意识到危机的严重性」，realized
the seriousness 属于无中生有，且 few 与原文的 many 也不符。
借用原文：address the effects of the global crisis
D) 原词陷阱
Many countries need support to improve their people's livelihood. 保住了 many
countries 这个和答案一样的开头，最易混；但 Somavia 说的是许多国家「没采取措施」，
不是「需要支持来改善民生」。need support、improve livelihood 都是原文未出现的内
容，属偷换。
借用原文：many countries have not done so
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Big fast food chains in New York City have started to obey a first-of-its-kind rule requiring them to
post calorie counts right on the menu. Cathy Nonas is with the New York City Department of Health.
纽约市的大型快餐连锁店已开始遵守一项首创性规定,要求它们直接在菜单上标注卡路里含量。Cathy
Nonas是纽约市卫生局的工作人员。
2 "We wanted to give people an opportunity to actually see the calories before they purchase the food
and make a decision, an informed decision that if they want to make the healthier choice, if they
want to eat fewer calories, they can. And we expect this will have a huge impact on obesity. And of
course, if it has an impact on obesity, it will have an impact on diabetes and heart disease and high
blood pressure."
我们希望让人们有机会在购买食物之前真正看到卡路里含量并做出决定,一个知情的决定,如果他们想做出
更健康的选择,如果他们想摄入更少的卡路里,他们就可以做到。我们预计这将对肥胖产生巨大影响。当然,
如果它对肥胖产生影响,它也将对糖尿病、心脏病和高血压产生影响。
3 The new rules were introduced as part of an anti-obesity campaign that also includes a recent citywide
ban on artificial trans fats in restaurant food. The menu rule only applies to restaurants that serve
standardised portion sizes and have fifteen or more locations nationwide.
这些新规定是作为抗肥胖运动的一部分推出的,该运动还包括最近在全市范围内禁止在餐厅食品中使用人工
反式脂肪。该菜单规定仅适用于提供标准化份量并在全国拥有十五家或更多门店的餐厅。
4 Starting last Saturday, chains big enough to fall under the rule will face penalties of up to 2000
dollars for not showing calorie information in a prominent spot on their menus, preferably next to
the price.
从上周六开始,规模足够大而受该规定约束的连锁店如果不在菜单的显著位置(最好在价格旁边)显示卡路里
信息,将面临最高2000美元的罚款。

questions.stem: What are big fast food chains in New York City required to do according to the new rule?
options: B) Put calorie information on the menu.
C) Increase protein content in the food.
D) Offer convenient food to customers.

explain.定位:
Big fast food chains in New York City have started to obey a first-of-its-kind rule requiring
them to post calorie counts right on the menu.
纽约市的大型快餐连锁店已开始遵守一项前所未有的规定，该规定要求它们把热量数值直接
标在菜单上。
explain.信号:
requiring 引出要求内容。信号词是 requiring them to（要求它们去……），它后面紧跟的
动作 post calorie counts right on the menu 就是"被要求做什么"的答案落点，听
到"requiring"就该锁定其后的动词。
explain.替换:
post calorie counts right on the menu ↔ Put calorie information on the menu
post=put、counts=information
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项里的"standardized""nationwide"录音确实念过，但 restaurants that serve
standardised portion sizes and have fifteen or more locations nationwide 说的是"哪
些餐厅受这条规定约束"的资格条件，不是"规定要求餐厅去做"的事。听到原词就选，正中圈
套。
借用原文：restaurants that serve standardised portion sizes and have fifteen or more
locations nationwide
C) 未提及
"protein content"（增加蛋白质含量）录音通篇没出现，是凭"健康饮食"的常识硬造的。规
定关心的是公示热量信息让人少摄入，而非改配方加蛋白质。
D) 偷换概念
"Offer convenient food"（提供便利食品）听着像"快餐"的合理引申，但录音的要求是"公
示热量"，从没要求餐厅去"提供便利食物"。这是把话题（快餐）替换成了一个文本里没有的
要求。

questions.stem: What will happen to big restaurant chains that violate the new rule?
options: C) They will get a warning.

explain.定位:
Starting last Saturday, chains big enough to fall under the rule will face penalties of up to
2000 dollars for not showing calorie information in a prominent spot on their menus,
preferably next to the price.
从上周六起，规模足以受该规定约束的连锁店，若未在菜单显眼处（最好紧挨价格）标出热
量信息，将面临最高 2000 美元的罚款。
explain.信号:
face penalties + 金额。信号是 will face penalties of up to 2000 dollars——"face
penalties"（面临处罚）加上明确金额"2000 dollars"，正是"违规后果"的落点；听到具体罚
款数字就该锁定这是答"会怎样"的句子。
explain.替换:
will face penalties of up to 2000 dollars ↔ They will be fined.
face penalties=be fined
explain.排除:
B) 过度推断
"They will be closed."（被关停）录音从没说，是把"罚款"这种处罚自行升级成"关店"。新
规明确的后果是最高 2000 美元罚款，并未到停业的程度。
C) 未提及
"They will get a warning."（被警告）听起来像处罚的一种，但录音说的是"face
penalties"（罚款），从未提"warning"。这是用一个文本没有的、更轻的后果来分散对"罚
款"的注意。
D) 未提及
"They will lose customers."（流失顾客）是从"公示热量可能吓退食客"的常识引申出来
的，但录音讲违规后果时只说罚款，并没提顾客流失。

questions.stem: What is the problem with many companies according to the news report?
options: A) Inability to implement their business plans.
B) Inability to keep turning out novel products.
C) Lack of a successful business model of their own.
D) Failure to integrate innovation into their business.

explain.定位:
Almost all companies recognize the importance of innovation today, but not many are able to
integrate innovation into their business.
如今几乎所有公司都认识到创新的重要性，但能把创新真正融入自身业务的公司却不多。
explain.信号:
转折 but 之后才是真意。这句以 but not many are able to integrate innovation into
their business 转折，but 前半句"都认识到创新重要"是铺垫，but 之后"能融入业务的不
多"才是录音想说的"问题"所在，转折后即答案落点。
explain.替换:
not many are able to integrate innovation into their business ↔
Failure to integrate innovation into their business.
not able to = Failure 否定转名词
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项 Inability to implement their business plans. 里的 business plans（商业计划）录音
从未出现，它只是借用 business 一词凑"经营"话题来诱选，属无中生有。
B) 原词陷阱
选项 Inability to keep turning out novel products. 用 novel products 呼应录音
creating something new，但那句是讲"人们对创新的误解"（第6题考点），不是"公司的
问题"，把别处原词搬到本题，属张冠李戴式原词陷阱。
借用原文：creating something new
C) 偷换概念
选项 Lack of a successful business model of their own. 借用录音末尾 business models
一词，但录音只在列举"创新可发生在产品、职能、商业模式、流程"时一笔带过，从没说公
司"缺少自己的成功模式"，属偷换概念。
借用原文：business models

questions.stem: What do many people tend to think of innovation?
options: A) It is the secret to business success.
B) It is the creation of something new.
C) It is a magic tool to bring big rewards.
D) It is an essential part of business culture.

explain.定位:
The article says many people tend to assume that innovation just means creating something
new, but actually it's more than that.
文章说，很多人往往以为创新就只是创造新东西，但实际上创新远不止于此。
explain.信号:
标志句 many people tend to assume。many people tend to assume that
innovation just means creating something new 用 many people tend to assume 这
一"人们倾向于认为"的标志，正面回答了题干"很多人怎么想"；其后 but actually it's more
than that 是作者纠偏，与本题问的"人们怎么想"无关。
explain.替换:
innovation just means creating something new ↔ It is the creation of something new.
creating → creation 动词转名词
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项 It is the secret to business success. 借了录音里反复出现的 success（a primary
tool for success），但那是讲"创新文化是成功工具"，回答的是"创新该是什么"而非"很多
人以为创新是什么"，属原词陷阱。
借用原文：a primary tool for success
C) 张冠李戴
选项 It is a magic tool to bring big rewards. 里的 big rewards 来自录音讲宝洁的 offers
big rewards for high-risk ideas，那是第7题宝洁部分的细节，与"很多人怎么想创新"无
关，属张冠李戴式原词陷阱。
借用原文：offers big rewards for high-risk ideas
D) 偷换概念
选项 It is an essential part of business culture. 借录音 develop an innovation culture
里的 culture，但那是文章/作者的主张，不是"很多人 tend to think"的内容；题干限定的
是"很多人怎么想"，故偷换了观点归属。
借用原文：develop an innovation culture

questions.stem: What does the company Procter&Gamble owe its success to?
options: D) Its willingness to make investments.

explain.定位:
The article cites the global giant Procter & Gamble as an example, saying a real innovative
company should develop an innovation culture and use it as a primary tool for success.
文章以全球巨头宝洁公司为例，说一家真正具有创新精神的公司应当培育创新文化，并把它
作为取得成功的首要工具。
explain.信号:
点名宝洁后紧跟"靠创新文化"。录音一点名 Procter & Gamble 作为例子，紧接着就说
develop an innovation culture and use it as a primary tool for success，把"创新文
化"和"成功的首要工具"直接挂钩，正是"宝洁靠什么成功"的答案句。
explain.替换:
develop an innovation culture and use it as a primary tool for success ↔ Its innovation culture.
原句详述 → 选项概括
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项 Its hardworking employees. 借录音里多次出现的 employees（a special
innovation facility for its employees），但录音只说宝洁为员工设了创新设施、让员工去
那里互动，从没说成功靠"员工勤奋"，hardworking 是无中生有，属原词陷阱。
借用原文：a special innovation facility for its employees
B) 未提及
选项 Its flexible promotion strategy. 说的"灵活的晋升/促销策略"录音里只字未提，
promotion 一词录音都没出现，纯属凭空捏造来填一个干扰项，属未提及。
D) 偷换概念
选项 Its willingness to make investments. 借录音 Corporate Innovation Fund 与 big
rewards 暗示"投钱"，但那只是创新文化的一个具体做法，录音把成功归于"创新文化"这个
整体，而非"愿意投资"本身，以偏概全、偷换概念。
借用原文：Corporate Innovation Fund

questions.stem: What does the man say about himself?
options: A) He's got addicted to technology.
B) He is not very good at socializing
C) He is crazy about text-messaging.
D) He does not talk long on the phone.

explain.定位:
But I get off the phone pretty quickly when I call. I'm not a big talker.
不过我打电话时挂得挺快的。我不是个话多的人。
explain.信号:
本人对自己的直接定性。这是男生评价自己的直接应答：I get off the phone pretty
quickly when I call 加上 I'm not a big talker，是他对『自己是怎样一个人』的当面陈
述，正对题干所问，因此是答案句。
explain.替换:
get off the phone pretty quickly ↔ does not talk long on the phone
挂得快=讲不久，肯定句改否定句
I'm not a big talker ↔ does not talk long on the phone
不是话多的人，补强不讲久
explain.排除:
A)
He's got addicted to technology.（沉迷科技）原文从未说过，男生只说自己打电话短、
不爱多聊，反而 I prefer to make a call 显示他用手机偏传统，谈不上沉迷，这是凭常识脑
补出来的过重表述。
B)
He is not very good at socializing（不擅社交）是对 I'm not a big talker 的过度引申：
『不爱多说』不等于『不会社交』，前者是讲话习惯、后者是社交能力，选项偷偷拔高了程
度。
借用原文：I'm not a big talker
C)
He is crazy about text-messaging. 盗用了原文反复出现的 text message 这个原词，但
『发短信多』的是女生 I text message a lot，男生明说 I don't do it so much，把女生的
特点安到了男生头上。
借用原文：I text message a lot

questions.stem: What does the woman tend to do while she is on the phone?

explain.定位:
If I call them, I'll have to have a long conversation.
如果我打电话给他们，我就不得不聊上很久。
explain.信号:
女生本人对打电话后果的自述。女生解释自己为何爱发短信时说 If I call them, I'll have to
have a long conversation，这是她对『一打电话就会怎样』的直接自述，正对题干所问的
打电话时的行为，是答案句。
explain.替换:
have a long conversation ↔ Talk at length
聊很久=说得久，同义改写
explain.排除:
A)
Talk big 与正确项 Talk at length 都以 Talk 开头，专骗听到 talk 就选的人。但 Talk big 是
『吹牛、说大话』，原文女生说的是聊得久，根本不是吹牛，意思对不上。
C)
Gossip a lot（爱说闲话）和『打电话聊很久』听上去沾边，容易凭感觉选。但原文只说会
聊得久 have a long conversation，并没说聊的是闲话八卦，属无中生有。
D)
Forget herself（忘乎所以）原文从头到尾没有任何对应，女生只谈打电话会聊很久，没说
会忘乎所以，纯属凭空添加。

questions.stem: Why did the man text message all his friends when he first got his cell phone?
options: A) He thought it was cool.
C) He wanted to stay connected with them.
D) He had an urgent message to send.

explain.定位:
When I first got my cell phone, I thought it was so cool to text message all my friends who
have one, and I was pretty fast with my thumb then.
我刚拿到手机那会儿，觉得给所有有手机的朋友发短信特别酷，那时候我大拇指打字还挺
快的。
explain.信号:
I thought 引出的动机句。男生用 I thought it was so cool to text message all my
friends 直接说出当初发短信的想法，I thought 是表态度/原因的标志，正对 Why 所问的
动机，是答案句。
explain.替换:
I thought it was so cool ↔ He thought it was cool
几乎原话，只是去掉强调词
explain.排除:
B)
He needed the practice. 像是从原文 I was pretty fast with my thumb then（那时打字
快）联想出来的，但『当时打字快』是结果，不是『为了练习才发短信』的原因，选项把动
机说反、说错了。
借用原文：I was pretty fast with my thumb then
C)
He wanted to stay connected with them.（想和朋友保持联系）符合常识，最诱人，但男
生给的原因是『觉得酷』 I thought it was so cool，并没说为了保持联系，这是用常识替
代了原文。
D)
He had an urgent message to send.（有紧急消息要发）原文完全没提，男生只说当初觉
得酷、就给所有朋友发，没有任何『紧急』的情节，属凭空添加的极端情境。

questions.stem: What does the woman's father think of text-messaging?
options: A) It poses a challenge to seniors.
B) It saves both time and money.
C) It is childish and unprofessional.
D) It is cool and convenient.

explain.定位:
He said he'd never text message. He thinks it's very childish and unprofessional to
text message.
他说他绝不会发短信。他觉得发短信很幼稚、很不专业。
explain.信号:
明确的贬义评价词。父亲的态度由女生转述给出：very childish and unprofessional 是两
个鲜明的贬义词，加上 he'd never text message 的强烈语气，清楚表明他对短信持否定态
度，是答案句。
explain.替换:
very childish and unprofessional ↔ It is childish and unprofessional.
评价词原样照搬
explain.排除:
A)
It poses a challenge to seniors.（对老人是种挑战）看似和『父亲』这种长辈话题沾边，
但原文父亲谈的是短信幼稚不专业，从没说短信对老年人是挑战，属无中生有。
B) 与原文相反
It saves both time and money.（省时省钱）是正面评价，但父亲态度是负面的 childish
and unprofessional，极性正好相反，且原文也没提省钱省时这回事。
D) 原词陷阱
It is cool and convenient.（又酷又方便）是正面评价，与父亲的负面态度完全相反。注意
cool 这个原词是录音里男生评价时用过的 so cool，被搬来诱你把它当成父亲的看法，实为
张冠李戴又反了极性。
借用原文：I thought it was so cool

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
options: A) He wants to change his job assignment.
B) He is unhappy with his department manager
C) He thinks he deserves extra pay for overtime.
D) He is often singled out for criticism by his boss

explain.定位:
M: Well, I'd like to talk to you about Tim Bond, the department manager.
男：嗯，我想跟你聊聊蒂姆·邦德，就是我们部门经理。
explain.信号:
来意句＝开门见山。男方一开口的来意句 I’d like to talk to you about Tim Bond, the
department manager 直接点出他是为部门经理而来，后文 he’s been making unrealistic
demands on you 又印证他对经理不满，两处合起来锁定他『不满主管』。
explain.替换:
talk to you about Tim Bond, the department manager ↔ unhappy with his department manager
找上门谈＝不满
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
他抱怨被派太多活 do all her work as well as mine，A 顺着 work 编出『想换工作内
容』，但他全程没说要换岗，只是嫌活多、嫌经理不公，属答非所问。
借用原文：do all her work as well as mine
C) 原词陷阱
录音确实提到加班 I’d done a lot of overtime，但他要的是早走，不是『额外加班费 extra
pay』；C 借 overtime 这个真词编出钱的诉求，原文根本没提报酬。
借用原文：I’d done a lot of overtime during the week
D) 过度推断
他说自己像被针对 I’ve been targeted to do all her work，指被指派过多活，D 却把
targeted 偷换成『常因 criticism 挨批』；原文从头到尾没有任何『批评』，是无中生有的
夸大。
借用原文：I feel like I’ve been targeted to do all her work as well as mine

questions.stem: What is the man's chief complaint?
options: A) His workload was much too heavy.
B) His immediate boss did not trust him
C) His colleagues often refused to cooperate.
D) His salary was too low for his responsibility

explain.定位:
M: Well, ever since Sandra left the department, I feel like I've been targeted to do all her work
as well as mine. I'm expected to attend too many meetings and I seem to be spending a lot of
my time doing unnecessary paperwork.
男：嗯，自从桑德拉离开部门后，我感觉自己被盯上了，要把她的活也一并干了。我被要求
参加太多会议，好像大把时间都耗在没必要的文书工作上。
explain.信号:
铺陈最细＝主诉。这段一连摆出三层活——do all her work as well as mine、attend too
many meetings、doing unnecessary paperwork，是全篇最密集的具体抱怨；后面 I’d
done a lot of overtime 又回扣『活多到要加班』，反复落在工作量上，正是 chief
complaint 的信号。
explain.替换:
do all her work as well as mine ↔ workload was much too heavy
干两份活＝活太重
spending a lot of my time doing unnecessary paperwork ↔ workload was much too heavy
时间全耗在文书＝量大
explain.排除:
B) 与原文相反
录音里女方明说经理很信任他 Mr. Bond has a lot of trust in you，B 却说『上司不信任
他』，正好反了；B 蹭了 trust 这个词却把极性颠倒。
借用原文：that’s a positive sign showing that Mr. Bond has a lot of trust in you
C) 张冠李戴
原文是他被叫去帮同事 help other colleagues finish their work，C 却说成『同事拒绝配
合他』，把帮与被帮的方向倒过来；原文没有任何同事不配合的内容。
借用原文：I was told to help other colleagues finish their work
D) 未提及
他抱怨的是活多、加班、不公，从头到尾没说工资 salary，D 的『薪资太低』是凭空添的，
属无中生有。

questions.stem: How does the woman interpret the fact that the man was asked to help his colleagues with their work?
options: A) He never knows how to refuse.
B) He is always ready to help others
C) His boss has a lot of trust in him.
D) His boss has no sense of fairness.

explain.定位:
W: But surely that's a positive sign showing that Mr. Bond has a lot of trust in you.
女：可这恰恰是个好兆头啊，说明邦德先生很信任你。
explain.信号:
转折 But＋女方正评。女方用 But surely that’s a positive sign 转折，把男方眼中的委屈反
过来评价成好事，紧接 a lot of trust in you——转折后的这句正面评价，就是『女方解
读』的答案信号。
explain.替换:
Mr. Bond has a lot of trust in you ↔ His boss has a lot of trust in him.
人称转换的近原话
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
A『他不会拒绝』和录音里女方对这件事的解读无关，倒像把后文该不该 say no 的话题挪
过来；女方此处的判断是信任，不是评价他性格不会拒绝。
B) 答非所问
『总是乐于助人』是对男方的夸，可题问的是女方怎么解读这件事，女方给的解读是『受信
任』而非夸他热心；B 把评价对象/角度安错了。
D) 与原文相反
『上司不公平 no sense of fairness』其实是男方的牢骚口径 other colleagues get to
leave early，女方恰恰反着说这是好事；D 把女方的正面解读颠倒成负面。
借用原文：other colleagues get to leave early, and they don’t have such a lot of work to do

questions.stem: What did the woman advise the man to do?
options: A) Put all his complaints in writing.
B) Wait and see what happens next.
C) Learn to say no when necessary.
D) Talk to his boss in person first.

explain.定位:
W: Well, at this stage, it would be better if you approached him directly. ... Why don't you
send an email requesting a meeting with him in private?
女：嗯，现阶段你最好直接去找他谈。……你何不发封邮件，约他私下见一面呢？
explain.信号:
双建议信号句。女方连用两个建议信号——it would be better if you approached him
directly 和 Why don’t you send an email requesting a meeting with him in private，
落点都是『直接、当面去找经理谈』，正是 advise 的答案信号。
explain.替换:
it would be better if you approached him directly ↔ Talk to his boss in person first.
directly＝in person
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
女方确实提到发邮件 send an email requesting a meeting，但邮件是用来『约见面』
的，不是 A 说的『把所有抱怨写成书面投诉』；A 借 email 的影子歪曲成 complaints in
writing。
借用原文：send an email requesting a meeting with him in private
B) 张冠李戴
『再观望 wait and see』出自男方收尾 I’ll see what happens from there，而题问的是女
方的建议；B 把男方的话当成女方的建议，张冠李戴。
借用原文：I'll send him an email to request a meeting, and I'll see what happens from there
C) 未提及
『该拒绝时学会说不』听着对症（他活太多），但女方全程没给这条建议，她只让他当面去
谈；C 是看似合理却原文未提的方案。

questions.stem: What is the speaker mainly talking about?
options: A) The importance of sleep to a healthy life.
B) Reasons for Americans' decline in sleep.
C) Some tips to improve the quality of sleep.
D) Diseases associated with lack of sleep.

explain.定位:
No matter how it happened, millions of Americans are putting their health, quality of life and
even length of life in danger.
不管它是怎么发生的，数百万美国人正把自己的健康、生活质量、甚至寿命置于危险之中。
explain.信号:
首段收束句总领全篇。millions of Americans are putting their health, quality of life
and even length of life in danger 是首段的收束句，把全篇基调定为「睡眠不足危及健
康」；再加第二段 New evidence shows why getting enough sleep is a top priority 强
调睡眠是头等大事——开头立题 + 后文反复证「睡眠对健康多重要」，主旨落在「睡眠对
健康生活的重要性」。
explain.替换:
putting their health, quality of life and even length of life in danger ↔
The importance of sleep to a healthy life.
正话反说同指重要性
why getting enough sleep is a top priority ↔ The importance of sleep
top priority 等于 importance
explain.排除:
B) 偷换概念
首段虽抛出 Was it because of the growing attraction of the Internet, video games
and endless TV channels? 问了下减少的原因，但紧接着就用 No matter how it
happened（不管怎么发生的）把原因撇开，全文重心根本不在「为什么减少」。盗用了开
头那句疑问来骗你，实则以偏概全。
借用原文：Was it because of the growing attraction of the Internet, video games and endless
TV channels?
C) 未提及
选项说「改善睡眠质量的技巧」，但录音通篇在讲缺觉的危害和睡好的益处，唯一沾边的只
有结尾 say good night sooner（早点睡）一句劝告，远谈不上一套 tips。属于录音基本没
展开的内容，被常识「健康文章总会给点建议」脑补出来了。
D) 原词陷阱
录音确实列了 higher blood pressure, heart attack, diabetes, weight gain 等缺觉相关疾
病，盗用这些扎眼的病名很诱人。但它们是用来论证「睡眠很重要」的证据，是手段不是落
脚点；把论据当主旨，范围比真主旨窄。
借用原文：People who sleep less tend to have higher blood pressure, heart attack, diabetes, weight
gain and other problems.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the talk about today's Americans?
options: B) They are changing their living habits.
C) They get less and less sleep.
D) They know the dangers of lack of sleep.

explain.定位:
Some 40% of Americans get less than seven hours of shut-eye on weeknights. For example,
sleep duration has declined from some eight hours in the 1950s to seven in recent years.
约有 40% 的美国人在工作日的夜晚睡眠不足七小时。比如，睡眠时长已从 1950 年代的约
八小时下降到近年的七小时。
explain.信号:
数字与下降趋势词。答案句靠两处信号锁定：一是数字 Some 40% of Americans get less
than seven hours，二是趋势动词 sleep duration has declined from some eight hours
in the 1950s to seven——declined、less than 都在说美国人睡得越来越少，这正是题问
的「美国人现状」。听力里数字句和「下降/上升」趋势句几乎必是考点，听到就该锁定。
explain.替换:
sleep duration has declined from some eight hours in the 1950s to seven in recent years ↔
They get less and less sleep.
具体降幅概括为越来越少
Some 40% of Americans get less than seven hours of shut-eye ↔ get less and less sleep
less than 印证睡得少
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项说美国人「更有健康意识」，但录音通篇在说他们睡得少、把健康置于危险，根本没夸
他们健康意识强。这是凭「现代人越来越注重健康」的常识脑补出来的，与录音事实正相
反。
B) 未提及
选项说美国人「正在改变生活习惯」，录音里美国人是被动地睡得越来越少，没有任何「他
们在主动改习惯」的表述。属常识脑补，原文无据。
D) 原词陷阱
录音确有 putting their health... in danger 和后文大量讲缺觉的危害，danger 这个词反复
出现，让 They know the dangers of lack of sleep. 很诱人。但录音说的是「危害存
在」，从没说「美国人知道这些危害」——盗用了 danger 原词，却把「危害本身」偷换成
了「他们懂得危害」。
借用原文：millions of Americans are putting their health, quality of life and even length of life
in danger

questions.stem: What does the speaker say will happen to people who lack sleep?
options: A) Their weight will go down.
B) Their mind function will deteriorate.
C) Their work efficiency will decrease.
D) Their blood pressure will rise.

explain.定位:
People who sleep less tend to have higher blood pressure, heart attack, diabetes, weight gain
and other problems.
睡得少的人往往血压更高，并伴有心脏病、糖尿病、体重增加等问题。
explain.信号:
睡得少的人会怎样的后果句。People who sleep less tend to have higher blood
pressure, heart attack, diabetes, weight gain 以「睡得少的人」开头、tend to have 引
出后果清单，主语和题干 people who lack sleep 完全对应，是承载答案的后果句。前文
high blood pressure has become an increasing problem 也单独点了血压，进一步加重
「血压升高」这条。
explain.替换:
higher blood pressure ↔ Their blood pressure will rise.
higher 等于 will rise
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
录音明明说缺觉者 weight gain（体重增加），选项却说 Their weight will go down.（体
重下降）。盗用了 weight 这个原词，方向却整个反了——听到 weight 就选，正中陷阱。
借用原文：weight gain
B) 张冠李戴
选项说「思维/脑功能会退化」，录音的后果清单是血压、心脏病、糖尿病、体重，并未提
脑功能或思维能力。第三段虽说缺觉会 decrease immune function，但那是免疫功能，不
是脑功能，别把 function 一词张冠李戴。
借用原文：there are higher levels of stress hormones in their bodies, which can decrease
immune function
C) 未提及
选项说「工作效率会下降」，凭常识非常合理，但录音的后果全是生理指标（血压、疾病、
体重），从没说工作效率。属于常识脑补、原文无据。

questions.stem: What is the first decision you should make in preparing to apply for a place at university?
options: A) How much you can afford to pay.
B) What course you are going to choose.
C) Which university you are going to apply to.
D) When you are going to submit your application.

explain.定位:
The first decision is your choice of course.
第一个决定是你对课程（专业）的选择。
explain.信号:
排序词 The first decision 直接点题。答案句靠排序信号锁定：The first decision is your
choice of course. 里的 The first decision 与题干 first decision 严丝合缝，是录音直接给
出"第一步"的句子，听到 first 就锁定其后接的内容。
explain.替换:
your choice of course ↔ What course you are going to choose.
名词短语改写成从句，词根一致
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项 How much you can afford to pay. 谈"能付多少钱"，录音通篇讲选课程、选学校、写
陈述，从未把费用作为申请的某个决定步骤提出，属无中生有。
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Which university you are going to apply to. 盗用了录音里 where to apply 这层意
思，但原文说它是 The next decision is where to apply.——是"下一步"，被偷换成了"第
一步"，答非所问。
借用原文：The next decision is where to apply.
D) 答非所问
选项 When you are going to submit your application. 对应录音 The deadline is
January 15th. 谈的"何时提交"，那是流程末端关于截止日期的提醒，不是题目所问的"第一
个决定"，属答非所问。
借用原文：The deadline is January 15th.

questions.stem: What is the most important part of the application?
options: A) The list of courses studied.
B) The full record of scores.

explain.定位:
The most important part of the application is the much feared personal statement.
申请中最重要的一部分，就是那份令人极为畏惧的个人陈述。
explain.信号:
最高级 The most important part 锁定。答案句靠最高级信号锁定：The most
important part of the application is the much feared personal statement. 与题干
most important part 完全对应，最高级后面接的 personal statement 即答案，无需综合
全篇。
explain.替换:
the much feared personal statement ↔ The personal statement.
去掉修饰，核心名词原样保留
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项 The list of courses studied. 借用了首段反复出现的 course 一词制造熟悉感，但录音
从未把"学过的课程清单"列为申请材料，更没说它最重要，属未提及。
借用原文：your choice of course
B) 未提及
选项 The full record of scores. 谈成绩单，听起来很合常理，但录音里并无"成绩"是申请材
料、更非"最重要"的说法，属未提及。
C) 未提及
选项 The references from teachers. 谈教师推荐信，是常见申请材料，但录音通篇未提
及"推荐信"，更未称其最重要，属未提及。

questions.stem: What must applicants do in their personal statements?
options: A) Specify what they would like to do after graduation.
B) Describe in detail how much they would enjoy studying.
C) Indicate they have reflected and thought about the subject.
D) Emphasize that they admire the professors in the university.

explain.定位:
They will look for evidence that you have reflected and thought about the subject.
他们（招生官）会寻找证据，看你是否对这门学科有过反思和思考。
explain.信号:
招生官"寻找"的内容即"必须做到"。答案句靠"要求信号"锁定：They will look for
evidence that you have reflected and thought about the subject. 中 look for
evidence 表明这是招生官要找的东西，即申请者必须在陈述里做到的，正面回答了题目。
explain.替换:
you have reflected and thought about the subject ↔
Indicate they have reflected and thought about the subject.
近乎照搬，仅人称与动词"显示"补足
They will look for evidence ↔ Indicate
"招生官找证据"="申请者要显示出来"
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项 Specify what they would like to do after graduation. 谈"毕业后想做什么"，录音里
关于个人陈述只字未提毕业去向的要求，属未提及。
B) 与原文相反
选项 Describe in detail how much they would enjoy studying. 盗用了录音里的 enjoy
一词，但原文明说 It is not convincing if you say you have chosen the subject because
you enjoy it.——只写"喜欢/享受"恰恰是不行的，选项把录音否定的做法当成了要求，与原
文相反。
借用原文：It is not convincing if you say you have chosen the subject because you enjoy it.
D) 未提及
选项 Emphasize that they admire the professors in the university. 谈"仰慕教授"，录音
通篇未出现 professors，也未要求陈述里写对教授的钦佩，属未提及。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the first motor car?
options: A) It was equipped with rubber tyres.
B) It was built in the late 19th century.
C) It was purchased by the Royal family.
D) It was designed by an English engineer.

explain.定位:
It is usually agreed that a German, Carl Benz, built the first motor car in 1885.
人们普遍认为，是一位德国人卡尔·本茨在 1885 年造出了第一辆机动车。
explain.信号:
开篇点题句给出年份。篇章第一句就交代了第一辆车的人和时间 built the first motor car
in 1885，开头点题句直接给出年份，这是细节题最好抓的定位信号——听到 1885 立刻把
它和选项里的年代对上。
explain.替换:
built the first motor car in 1885 ↔ It was built in the late 19th century.
1885 = 19 世纪后期
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
It was equipped with rubber tyres. 盗用了录音 rubber tyres 这个原词，但那是第二段讲
1905 年的车才有的特征，被安到了第一辆车头上，时间和对象都对不上。
借用原文：rubber tyres
C) 原词陷阱
It was purchased by the Royal family. 盗用了 the Royal family 原词，但录音说的是皇室
成员把开车当成一种运动 took up motoring as a sport，并没说他们买下了第一辆车，属
答非所问。
借用原文：took up motoring as a sport
D) 与原文相反
It was designed by an English engineer. 与录音相反：原文明说造车人是德国人 a
German, Carl Benz，选项却换成 English，国籍被偷偷改掉。
借用原文：a German, Carl Benz

questions.stem: What was the problem with the early cars in Britain?
options: A) They consumed lots of petrol.
B) They took two passengers only.
C) They were difficult to drive.

explain.定位:
There were no petrol pumps and few garages, so every driver had to be his own engineer for
the frequent breakdowns.
当时没有加油站、车库也很少，所以每个司机都得自己当工程师，应付频繁的故障。
explain.信号:
so 引出后果，落点在 breakdowns。录音用 so 把缺乏配套设施引向后果——司机得自
己修"frequent breakdowns"，so every driver had to be his own engineer for the
frequent breakdowns 中 so 之后才是真正交代"问题"的落点，听到 so + 麻烦后果就
锁定。
explain.替换:
the frequent breakdowns ↔ They often broke down.
frequent breakdowns = often broke down
explain.排除:

questions.stem: Many people feel guilty when they cannot find a place other than a nursing home for their parents.
questions.passage:
Finding the Right Home—and Contentment, Too

A) When your elderly relative needs to enter some sort of long-term care facility—a moment few parents or children approach without fear-what you would like is to have everything made clear.

B) Does assisted living really mark a great improvement over a nursing home, or has the industry simply hired better interior designers? Are nursing homes as bad as people fear, or is that an out-moded stereotype(固定看法)? Can doing one's homework really steer families to the best places? It is genuinely hard to know.

C) I am about to make things more complicated by suggesting that what kind of facility an older person lives in may matter less than we have assumed. And that the characteristics adult children look for when they begin the search are not necessarily the things that make a difference to the people who are going to move in. I am not talking about the quality of care, let me hastily add. Nobody flourishes in a gloomy environment with irresponsible staff and a poor safety record. But an accumulating body of research indicates that some distinctions between one type of elder care and another have little real bearing on how well residents do.

Russell argues that as robots take on more complicated tasks, it's necessary to translate our morals into AI language.

For example, if a robot does chores around the house, you wouldn't want it to put the pet cat in the oven to make dinner for the hungry children. "You would want that robot preloaded with a good set of values," said Russell.

It will be possible to create more sophisticated moral machines, if only we can find a way to set out human values as clear rules.

Robots could also learn values from drawing patterns from large sets of data on human behavior. They are dangerous only if programmers are careless.

The biggest concern with robots going against human values is that human beings fail to do sufficient testing and they've produced a system that will break some kind of taboo(禁忌).

One simple check would be to program a robot to check the correct course of action with a human when presented with an unusual situation.

If the robot is unsure whether an animal is suitable for the microwave, it has the opportunity to stop, send out beeps(嘟嘟声), and ask for directions from a human. If we humans aren't quite sure about a decision, we go and ask somebody else.

The most difficult step in programming values will be deciding exactly what we believe is moral, and how to create a set of ethical rules. But if we come up with an answer, robots could be good for humanity.

B) To find out if one's lifestyle has any effect on their health

questions.passage:
Why do some people live to be older than others? You know the standard explanations:keeping a moderate diet, engaging in regular exercise, etc. But what effect does your personality have on your longevity(长寿)? Do some kinds of personalities lead to longer lives? A new study in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society looked at this question by examining the personality characteristics of 246 children of people who had lived to be at least 100.

The study shows that those living the longest are more outgoing, more active and less neurotic(神经质的) than other people. Long-living women are also more likely to be sympathetic and cooperative than women with a normal life span. These findings are in agreement with what you would expect from the evolutionary theory: those who like to make friends and help others can gather enough resources to make it through tough times.

Interestingly, however, other characteristics that you might consider advantageous had no impact on whether study participants were likely to live longer. Those who were more self-disciplined, for instance, were no more likely to live to be very old. Also, being open to new ideas had no relationship to long life, which might explain all those bad-tempered old people who are fixed in their ways.

Whether you can successfully change your personality as an adult is the subject of a longstanding psychological debate. But the new paper suggests that if you want long life, you should strive to be as outgoing as possible.

Unfortunately, another recent study shows that your mother's personality may also help determine your longevity. That study looked at nearly 28,000 Norwegian mothers and found that those moms who were more anxious, depressed and angry were more likely to feed their kids unhealthy diets. Patterns of childhood eating can be hard to break when we're adults, which may mean that kids of depressed moms end up dying younger.

Personality isn't destiny(命运), and everyone knows that individuals can learn to change. But both studies show that long life isn't just a matter of your physical health but of your mental health.

You know the standard explanations:keeping a moderate diet, engaging in regular exercise, etc. But what effect does your personality have on your longevity(长寿)? Do some kinds of personalities lead to longer lives? A new study in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society looked at this question by examining the personality characteristics of 246 children of people who had lived to be at least 100.

The study shows that those living the longest are more outgoing, more active and less neurotic(神经质的) than other people. Long-living women are also more likely to be sympathetic and cooperative than women with a normal life span. These findings are in agreement with what you would expect from the evolutionary theory: those who like to make friends and help others can gather enough resources to make it through tough times.

Interestingly, however, other characteristics that you might consider advantageous had no impact on whether study participants were likely to live longer. Those who were more self-disciplined, for instance, were no more likely to live to be very old. Also, being open to new ideas had no relationship to long life, which might explain all those bad-tempered old people who are fixed in their ways.

Whether you can successfully change your personality as an adult is the subject of a longstanding psychological debate. But the new paper suggests that if you want long life, you should strive to be as outgoing as possible.

Unfortunately, another recent study shows that your mother's personality may also help determine your longevity. That study looked at nearly 28,000 Norwegian mothers and found that those moms who were more anxious, depressed and angry were more likely to feed their kids unhealthy diets. Patterns of childhood eating can be hard to break when we're adults, which may mean that kids of depressed moms end up dying younger.

Personality isn't destiny(命运), and everyone knows that individuals can learn to change. But both studies show that long life isn't just a matter of your physical health but of your mental health.

writing.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a letter to express your thanks to one of your school teachers upon entering college. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.model:
Dear Mr. Wang,
Now that I have entered college, I am writing to express my heartfelt thanks to you for all the guidance you
gave me during my high school years.
I still clearly remember the time when I failed an important English exam and almost gave up. Instead of
blaming me, you stayed after class, went through every mistake with me, and encouraged me to keep trying. It
was you who helped me build the habit of reading English news every morning, which has greatly improved
my language skills and confidence. Thanks to your patience and faith in me, I finally earned a place at my
dream university.
I owe much of my progress to you, and I will always treasure what you taught me, both in knowledge and in
character. I sincerely wish you good health and happiness in the years ahead.
Yours sincerely, Li Ming

translation.source: 功夫 (Kung Fu)是中国武术 (martial arts)的俗称。中国武术的起源可以追溯到自卫的需要、狩猎活动以及古代中国的军事训练。它是中国传统体育运动的一种，年轻人和老年人都练。它已逐渐演变成了中国文化的独特元素。作为中国的国宝， 功夫有上百种不同的风格，是世界上练得最多的武术形式。有些风格模仿了动物的动作， 还有一些则受到了中国哲学思想、神话和传说的启发。
translation.reference: Kung Fu is the popular name for Chinese martial arts. The origins of Chinese martial arts can be traced back to the need for self-defense, hunting activities and ancient Chinese military training. It is a form of traditional Chinese sports practiced by both the young and the old. It has gradually evolved into a unique element of Chinese culture. As a national treasure of China, Kung Fu has hundreds of different styles and is the most practiced martial art form in the world. Some styles imitate the movements of animals, while others are inspired by Chinese philosophy, mythology and legends.
